what_this_is: Cross-check for the Artificial Analysis API pull: the public artificialanalysis.ai pages, read with Firecrawl (not the API) on 17 October 2026. Every value is copied from the page, with the URL and the exact sentence, card, table cell or chart label it came from.
how_it_was_read: Each model page was read twice with Firecrawl scrape, maxAge 0 (live fetch): once as markdown plus raw HTML, and once as rendered markdown after a 6 second wait so the chart bar labels appear.

Score and cost per task come from the page's own sentences ("... scores N on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index ..." and "On average, it costs $X per task to evaluate ... on the Intelligence Index."), cross-checked against the summary card and, for scores, the release page table cell.

The cost to run the whole index appears on the page only as a bar label on the chart "Cost to Run Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index". The bar for this model was found by position: the chart lists its linked models in bar order and prints one total per bar. That mapping was accepted only when every bar's label on the chart equalled that model's total in the page's embedded data, rounded to whole dollars.
Unrounded values are copied from the page's embedded data (the data the charts draw from). They are not visible text and should be cited only as 'unrounded figure in the page data'.
Raw page copies are in /home/user/content-engine/.cache/visual-intel/aa-pages; scripts in /home/user/content-engine/.cache/visual-intel/scripts.

index_definition.title: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2
index_definition.scale_sentence: The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is calculated as a weighted average of production benchmark scores, scaled from 0 to 100. Four categories each contribute 25%: agents, coding, general capability, and scientific reasoning.
index_definition.what_it_measures_sentence: The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is a composite benchmark score that measures language model capabilities across reasoning, coding, knowledge, instruction following, scientific reasoning, and completing multi-step tasks.
index_definition.evaluations_sentence: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 incorporates 10 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1
index_definition.methodology_weighting_sentence: Intelligence Index is calculated as a weighted average across four categories: Agents (30%), Coding (20%), Scientific Reasoning (20%) and General (30%). The weighting emphasizes agentic tasks. Category membership and per-evaluation weights are shown below.
index_definition.conflict: The two AA pages disagree on the category weights. The index page FAQ says 'Four categories each contribute 25%'; the methodology page says 'Agents (30%), Coding (20%), Scientific Reasoning (20%) and General (30%)'. The methodology table (per-evaluation weights) adds up to the 30/20/20/30 split. Cite the methodology page if weights are mentioned.

cost_per_task.chart_subtitle: Weighted average cost (USD) per Intelligence Index task · Lower is better
cost_per_task.definition_sentence: Weighted average cost per Intelligence Index task. Each evaluation’s cost is calculated from input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning, and answer token prices, divided by task count, and weighted by its Intelligence Index weight.

cost_to_run_index.chart_subtitle: Cost (USD) to run all evaluations in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
cost_to_run_index.definition_sentence: The cost to run the evaluations in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, calculated using the model's input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning, and answer token prices and the number of tokens used across evaluations (excluding repeats).

cost_definitions.methodology_sentence: For the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index evaluations, we use the token counts reported by each model's API provider where available, to accurately report the cost of running the Intelligence Index. In the rare cases where provider token counts are unavailable, we use a canonical-tokenizer fallback. This contrasts with the approach in performance benchmarking, where we use client-side token counts from the `o200k_base` tokenizer to standardize token counts for the same text across models. When reporting cache hit rates and cost, we combine these token counts with live measurements of the model's typical cache hit rate, rather than relying on the one-off measurement when the evaluation was run.
cost_definitions.price_basis: Model pages say prices are 'based on Anthropic's API' (or the maker's own API) and list input and output prices per million tokens. The methodology adds that cost combines provider token counts 'with live measurements of the model's typical cache hit rate'. So these are list-price costs including AA's cache assumption, not what any customer was billed.
